text:
infra-bot: [PERF-CHECK] master perf job failing: continuous-batcher token/sec ~22% below baseline. Job: perf/continuous-batcher. https://ci.redwood/devices/perf/7890

Matt G.: that looks like the merge I landed yesterday afternoon (PR #3124). I tweaked kernel fallback order + prefetch threshold.

Anya Patel: noticed the alert too — canary shows token/sec drop on 3/6 canary nodes. tail latency nominal, but sustained throughput under medium load drops. tagging runtime owners. :eyes: 

Samir: grabbing perf samples. initial flamegraphs show large memcpy hotspots only on the new kernel path. KV hitrate stable. suspect extra buffer copies during coalesce/pack.

Lee: is the memcpy host->device or intra-host? paste the perf snippet when you have it.

Samir: condensed profile from perf run:

```
  40.2%  runtime  [.] memcpy_avx
   8.7%  scheduler [.] coalesce_batches
   6.5%  serving   [.] serialize_kv_for_kernel
   4.9%  driver    [.] launch_kernel_variant
```

Samir: memcpy spike correlates with kernel-variant-B. variant-A (older path) doesn't show that hotspot.

Matt G.: kernel-variant-B uses a new packing layout and slightly different prefetching; I made it preferred for mid-length seqs in the fallback ordering.

Anya Patel: that maps: packing -> different memory layout -> extra copies during coalescing. Our batcher now hits the path more often so aggregate memcopies increase, reducing token/sec.

Lee: can we narrow to the exact commit in PR #3124? if it's just the packing change we can revert that chunk or introduce a targeted bypass.

Matt G.: starting git bisect now on the merged branch.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout for release/2026-03-16 paused due to perf regression. Affected routes: text.generate.medium, chat.multi-turn.

Matt G.: bisect results: bad = merge 0a1b2c3, good = a9b8c7d. Culprit: commit 1f2e3d4 — "kernel: packing layout + prefetch tweak".

Samir: local validation: forcing variant-A -> token/sec matches baseline. forcing variant-B -> token/sec down ~20% and memcpy_avx spikes.

Anya Patel: options: full revert of packing change (fast) or surgical guard in coalesce to skip extra copies when not needed (more surgical). Revert loses pack gains for long seqs.

Matt G.: revert is safe (internal changes), no external API impact. I can push revert hotfix if needed. But prefer minimal change if it's quick.

Lee: quick idea: add an is_contiguous check before pack_copy() in coalesce. If buffer already contiguous and aligned, skip packing. Cheap guard.

Samir: I'll prototype that check. if buffer.contiguous && (alignment % 64 == 0) -> bypass pack_copy(). Should reduce memcpy frequency.

Matt G.: sounds good. push a tiny PR with the guard + unit test and perf CI. I'll stand by to open a revert if CI/ canary still fails.

Samir: pushed branch feature/avoid-extra-pack-copy. Quick perf run locally: token/sec within ~+2% of baseline, memcpy_avx back to normal.

Matt G.: opened PR 3140: https://git.redwood/r/redwood/serving/pulls/3140 — short-circuit pack_copy when payload already contiguous. Includes unit test and perf CI link.

infra-bot: queued perf CI for PR 3140. compare: https://ci.redwood/devices/perf/3140/compare

Anya Patel: plan: if perf CI looks good, canary the PR to the three affected nodes and monitor token/sec for 30m before unpausing rollout. I'll coordinate with platform.

deploy-bot: Canary for PR 3140 scheduled on zone-us-west-2 nodes c-03,c-07,c-11 at 16:10 UTC.

infra-bot: perf CI for 3140 passed: token/sec delta +1% vs baseline; memcpy hotspot not present. https://ci.redwood/devices/perf/3140/result

Anya Patel: great. proceed with canary. Holding note: follow-up RFC to redesign packing to be copy-free for common-case contiguous KV layouts, and measure long-seq alignment benefit we temporarily lost.

Matt G.: merging PR 3140 now. I'll draft the RFC for a copyless packing design next sprint.

Samir: added reproduction steps in PR and the perf test configs that are sensitive: batch sizes 8-16, seq lengths 256-1024.

Lee: nice turnaround. thanks all. :thumbsup:
